source_text: μόσχων καὶ πρωτότοκα προβάτων, καὶ πρωτότοκα αἰγῶν οὐ λυτρώσῃ· ἅγιά ἐστι· καὶ τὸ αἷμα αὐτῶν προσχεεῖς πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καὶ τὸ στέαρ ἀνοίσεις κάρπωμα εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ. Καὶ τὰ κρέα ἔσται σοὶ, καθὰ καὶ τὸ στηθύνιον τοῦ ἐπιθέματος· καὶ κατὰ τὸν βραχίονα τὸν δεξιὸν, σοὶ ἔσται. Πᾶν ἀφαίρεμα τῶν ἁγίων, ὅσα ἐὰν ἀφέλωσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ Κυρίῳ, δέδωκα σοὶ καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς σου καὶ ταῖς θυγατράσι σου μετὰ σοῦ, νόμιμον αἰώνιον· διαθήκη ἁλὸς αἰωνίου ἐστὶν ἔναντι Κυρίου, σοὶ καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σέ.» Συνίης οὖν ἄρα κἀντεῦθεν, οἶμαί που, καὶ μάλα σαφῶς, ὅτι πᾶν εἶδος θυσίας καὶ προσαγωγῆς ἐκνενέμηκεν ἐναργῶς τῷ ἱερῷ τε καὶ ἀπολέκτῳ γένει, καὶ τὰ ἀπὸ πάσης πλημμελείας, καὶ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὰ ὑπὲρ πάσης πλημμελείας καὶ ἁμαρτίας θύματα. Ὄνομα γὰρ τοῖς ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας θύμασιν, ἁμαρτία. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ Παῦλος ἡμῖν ὁ σοφὸς, νομικὴν ἐπὶ Χριστῷ τὴν λέξιν ἐπετίθει λέγων· «Δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, καταλλάγητε τῷ Θεῷ· τὸν γὰρ μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησε.» Τέθυται γὰρ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, κατὰ τὰς Γραφὰς, ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον ὁ Υἱός. Ὅτι δὲ ἁμαρτία τοῖς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίας θύμασιν ὄνομα τέθειται παρὰ τοῦ νόμου, σαφηνιεῖ λέγων διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Θεὸς περὶ τῶν ἱερουργῶν· «Ἁμαρτίας λαοῦ μου φάγονται·» τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὰ ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν τοῦ λαοῦ μου, βρῶσις ἔσται τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν. Ἀπονέμει τοίνυν αὐτοῖς ἁπάσης θυσίας λείψανον, ἐδώδιμά τε ποιεῖσθαι προστάττει, πλὴν ἐν ἁγίῳ τόπῳ, φησὶ, καὶ ὑπὸ παντὸς ἀρσενικοῦ. Καὶ τίς ὁ ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγος, εἴρηται πρὸς ἡμῶν. Ἐν δὴ τοῖς ἤδη παρῳχηκόσιν, ἐλαίου δὲ ἀπαρχὴ, σίτου τε καὶ οἴνου, καὶ τῶν πρωτοτόκων αἱ ἀπολυτρώσεις, καὶ μέν τοι τὰ ἀναθήματα μόνοις οὐκέτι τοῖς ἀρσενικοῖς, οὐδὲ ἐν αὐλῇ τῇ ἁγία βρώσιμα, ἀλλ' ἐν οἴκῳ λοιπὸν ἱερέως, καὶ αὐταῖς θυγατράσιν ἐγκείμενα πρὸς ἀπόλαυσιν, καὶ παντὶ γνωρίμῳ καὶ οἰκειοτάτῳ. Καὶ ἀναγκαία πρὸς ἐπιτήρησι ἡ διαστολή· τὰ μὲν γὰρ τῶν θυσιῶν λείψανα, μόνου ἂν πρέποι τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις εἰς χρῆσιν, καὶ οὐχ ὡς βρῶσις ἔσται κοινή· καὶ τόπος ἅγιος, ὁ πρέπων αὐτοῖς. Τὰ δὲ ὅσα περίεστιν, ἐν δωροφορίας τάξει προσενηνεγμένα, παραλαβὼν, δεύτερόν πως, φησὶν, ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἔχει λόγον· καὶ παντὶ προσκείσεται τῷ οἴκῳ τοῖς ἱερουργοῖς, εἰ μόνον εἴη καθαρὸς, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἀβέβηλος· κατὰ μὲν τὸν νόμον, εἰ μὴ ἀπερίτμητος, εἰ μὴ ἀλλογενὴς, εἰ μὴ λεπρὸς, εἰ μὴ γονοῤῥυής· κατὰ δέ γε τὸν τοῦ νέου Γράμματος σκοπὸν καὶ ἀσφάλειαν ἐκκλησιαστικὴν, εἰ μὴ ἀνίερός τε καὶ ἄπιστος, εἰ εὐσεβὴς καὶ φιλόθεος. Πρέποι γὰρ ἂν ὅτι μάλιστά γε τοῖς εἰς θείαν ἱερουργίαν ἠγμένοις, κολλᾶσθαι φιλεῖν τοὺς οἵπερ ἂν εἶεν ἀγαθοί τε τὴν ἕξιν, καὶ φιλοθεΐας ἔμπλεω τὴν διάνοιαν ἔχοντες. pass_b_english: Cyril: …of calves, the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall pour their blood against the altar, and offer up the fat as a burnt offering, for a fragrant aroma to the Lord. And their meat shall be yours, like the breast of the wave offering; and like the right shoulder it shall be yours. Every portion set apart from the holy things, whatever the sons of Israel set apart for the Lord, I have given to you and to your sons and your daughters with you, a perpetual ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord, for you and your offspring after you’ (Numbers 18:17–19). From this too, then, you see quite clearly, I think, that he has plainly assigned every kind of sacrifice and offering to the sacred and chosen race, including what comes ‘from every trespass and from all the sins’, that is, the victims offered for every trespass and sin. For the victims offered for sin bear the name ‘sin’. That is why our wise Paul also applied the law’s word to Christ, saying: ‘We beseech you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God; for him who knew no sin he made sin for us’ (2 Corinthians 5:20–21). For the Son was sacrificed for our sins according to the Scriptures (1 Corinthians 15:3), as an innocent lamb (Jeremiah 11:19). That the law gave the name ‘sin’ to the victims offered for our sin, God will make clear when he says through the prophet concerning the priests: ‘They shall eat the sins of my people’ (Hosea 4:8); that is, what is offered for the sins of my people shall be food for the priests. So he assigns to them what remains of every sacrifice, and commands that it be eaten, but only in a holy place, he says, and by every male (Numbers 18:10; Leviticus 7:6). The reason for this we have given in what has gone before. But the firstfruits of oil, grain and wine, the payments for redeeming the firstborn, and the devoted things as well, are to be eaten no longer by the males alone, nor in the holy court, but now in the priest’s house; they are set there for the enjoyment even of his daughters, and of everyone close to him and of his own household. This distinction must be carefully observed. For the remains of the sacrifices would be fitting for the use of the consecrated alone, and will not be common food; and a holy place is the place that befits them. But whatever else is left over, having been brought as a gift, holds, one might say, a second rank of its own once the priest has received it; and it will belong to the priests’ whole household, if only the person is clean, that is, not profane: according to the law, if he is not uncircumcised, not a foreigner, not a leper, not one with a discharge (Leviticus 22:4, 10); but according to the aim of the new Scripture and the Church’s safeguard, if he is not unholy and unbelieving, if he is devout and loves God. For it would be most fitting for those brought into the divine priestly service to love to keep close company with people who are good in character and whose minds are full of love for God. And by adding to this, ‘It is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord, for you and your offspring with you’ (Numbers 18:19), he has commanded that what he also said elsewhere be kept without fail (Leviticus 2:13): ‘The salt of the covenant of the Lord shall not be lacking from your sacrifices. choices.why: τοῖς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίας θύμασιν rendered 'the victims offered for our sin' (ἡμῶν kept).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-quotation (Numbers 18:17–19, continued from section 29); the closing quotation mark and citation stand at the end of 18:19. In the quotation the covenant is 'for you and your offspring after you' (μετὰ σέ); when Cyril repeats it later the source reads 'with you' (μετὰ σοῦ); both kept as written. ἀφαίρεμα / ἀφέλωσιν rendered 'portion set apart / set apart' (the heave offering). 'Victims offered for sin bear the name sin': in the LXX the sin offering is often called simply ἁμαρτία, which is the ground of Cyril's reading of 2 Corinthians 5:21. 'Sacrificed for our sins according to the Scriptures' echoes 1 Corinthians 15:3 (Cyril has τέθυται, 'was sacrificed', for Paul's ἀπέθανεν, 'died'). 'Innocent lamb' (ἀρνίον ἄκακον) is the exact phrase of LXX Jeremiah 11:19 (ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον ἀγόμενον τοῦ θύεσθαι), so it is cited. Hosea 4:8 is a rebuke in its setting; Cyril uses only its wording. 'Only in a holy place … by every male' paraphrases Numbers 18:10, which says 'in the Holy of Holies'. Punctuation: Migne puts a full stop before Ἐν δὴ τοῖς ἤδη παρῳχηκόσιν, but the δέ after ἐλαίου shows the new clause begins there, so the phrase is read with the preceding sentence ('The reason for this we have given in what has gone before'). ἐπιτήρησι in the source is read as ἐπιτήρησιν. Doubtful: παραλαβὼν (masculine nominative singular) has no clear subject in 'Τὰ δὲ ὅσα περίεστιν … παραλαβὼν, δεύτερόν πως, φησὶν, ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἔχει λόγον'; it is rendered 'once the priest has received it', and φησίν is rendered 'one might say', since no Scripture is being quoted; the text may be corrupt here. Leviticus 22:4 (leper, man with a discharge) and 22:10 (no foreigner may eat the holy things) are cited; 'uncircumcised' comes from Exodus 12:43–48 (the Passover) and is left uncited, since Leviticus 22 does not name it. τοῦ νέου Γράμματος rendered 'the new Scripture'. Leviticus 2:13 quotation runs on into section 31 ('…offer salt to the Lord your God'); its citation is placed before the quotation because the quotation ends in the next section. τοῖς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίας θύμασιν rendered 'the victims offered for our sin' (ἡμῶν kept). 'Only in a holy place … by every male' matches Leviticus 7:6 (the trespass offering: 'every male among the priests shall eat it; in a holy place it shall be eaten') word for word, so it is cited beside Numbers 18:10.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (Greek tags moved to lemmas[]; English sense kept word for word in pass_a_gloss): [cont. Num 18:17–19 LXX] μόσχων, προβάτων, αἰγῶν πρωτότοκα οὐ λυτρώσῃ· ἅγιά ἐστι 'firstborn of calves, sheep, goats you shall not ransom; holy they are'; τὸ αἷμα προσχεεῖς πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον 'pour the blood against the altar', τὸ στέαρ ἀνοίσεις κάρπωμα εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας 'offer up the fat as a burnt offering for an odour of fragrance'; τὰ κρέα ἔσται σοί, καθὰ καὶ τὸ στηθύνιον τοῦ ἐπιθέματος 'the meat yours, as the breast of the wave offering', κατὰ τὸν βραχίονα τὸν δεξιόν 'as the right shoulder'; πᾶν ἀφαίρεμα τῶν ἁγίων, ὅσα ἀφέλωσιν 'every portion taken off of the holy things, whatever they take off'; διαθήκη ἁλὸς αἰωνίου ἔναντι Κυρίου 'covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord', σοὶ καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σέ 'to you and your seed after you'. Συνίης κἀντεῦθεν, οἶμαί που, καὶ μάλα σαφῶς 'you understand from here too, I suppose, very clearly' ὅτι πᾶν εἶδος θυσίας καὶ προσαγωγῆς ἐκνενέμηκεν ἐναργῶς τῷ ἱερῷ τε καὶ ἀπολέκτῳ γένει 'he has evidently allotted every kind of sacrifice and offering to the holy and chosen race', καὶ τὰ ἀπὸ πάσης πλημμελείας καὶ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὰ ὑπὲρ πάσης πλημμελείας καὶ ἁμαρτίας θύματα 'that is, the victims for every trespass and sin'. Ὄνομα γὰρ τοῖς ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας θύμασιν, ἁμαρτία 'for the name for victims for sin is sin'. Τοιγάρτοι Παῦλος ὁ σοφὸς νομικὴν ἐπὶ Χριστῷ τὴν λέξιν ἐπετίθει 'applied the legal term to Christ': 2 Cor 5:20–21 Δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, καταλλάγητε τῷ Θεῷ· τὸν μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησε. Τέθυται ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς 'was sacrificed for our sins according to the Scriptures', ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον ὁ Υἱός 'the Son as an innocent lamb'. ὅτι ἁμαρτία ... ὄνομα τέθειται παρὰ τοῦ νόμου 'that sin has been set as name by the law', σαφηνιεῖ λέγων διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Θεὸς περὶ τῶν ἱερουργῶν 'God will make clear saying through the prophet about the officiants': Ἁμαρτίας λαοῦ μου φάγονται 'they will eat the sins of my people'; τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὰ ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν τοῦ λαοῦ μου βρῶσις ἔσται 'what is for sins of my people will be food'. Ἀπονέμει ἁπάσης θυσίας λείψανον 'he allots the remnant of every sacrifice', ἐδώδιμα ποιεῖσθαι προστάττει 'commands it be made food', πλὴν ἐν ἁγίῳ τόπῳ καὶ ὑπὸ παντὸς ἀρσενικοῦ 'only in a holy place and by every male'. τίς ὁ ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγος εἴρηται πρὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τοῖς ἤδη παρῳχηκόσιν 'what the reason for this is has been said by us in what has passed'. ἐλαίου δὲ ἀπαρχή, σίτου, οἴνου, τῶν πρωτοτόκων αἱ ἀπολυτρώσεις 'ransomings of the firstborn', τὰ ἀναθήματα 'the devoted things' μόνοις οὐκέτι τοῖς ἀρσενικοῖς 'no longer for males only', οὐδὲ ἐν αὐλῇ τῇ ἁγίᾳ βρώσιμα 'nor eatable in the holy court', ἀλλ' ἐν οἴκῳ λοιπὸν ἱερέως 'but henceforth in the priest's house', καὶ αὐταῖς θυγατράσιν ἐγκείμενα πρὸς ἀπόλαυσιν 'laid up for enjoyment even for daughters', καὶ παντὶ γνωρίμῳ καὶ οἰκειοτάτῳ 'and every familiar and closest one'. ἀναγκαία πρὸς ἐπιτήρησιν ἡ διαστολή 'the distinction is necessary for observance'. τὰ τῶν θυσιῶν λείψανα μόνου ἂν πρέποι τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις εἰς χρῆσιν 'remnants of sacrifices fit for use of the consecrated only', οὐχ ὡς βρῶσις κοινή 'not as common food'; τόπος ἅγιος ὁ πρέπων. Τὰ δὲ ὅσα περίεστιν, ἐν δωροφορίας τάξει προσενηνεγμένα 'whatever remains, brought in the order of gift-bearing', παραλαβών 'having received' (masc. nom., subject unclear), δεύτερόν πως, φησίν, ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἔχει λόγον 'has in itself somehow a second rank'; παντὶ προσκείσεται τῷ οἴκῳ τοῖς ἱερουργοῖς 'will be assigned to all the house of the officiants', εἰ μόνον εἴη καθαρός, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἀβέβηλος 'if only he be clean, that is, not profane': κατὰ τὸν νόμον, εἰ μὴ ἀπερίτμητος, ἀλλογενής, λεπρός, γονοῤῥυής 'not uncircumcised, foreigner, leper, with discharge'; κατὰ τὸν τοῦ νέου Γράμματος σκοπὸν καὶ ἀσφάλειαν ἐκκλησιαστικήν 'by the aim of the new Writing and ecclesiastical safety', εἰ μὴ ἀνίερός τε καὶ ἄπιστος, εἰ εὐσεβὴς καὶ φιλόθεος 'if not unholy and faithless, if pious and God-loving'. Πρέποι ... τοῖς εἰς θείαν ἱερουργίαν ἠγμένοις κολλᾶσθαι φιλεῖν 'fitting for those led into divine sacred service to love to cleave to' those ἀγαθοὶ τὴν ἕξιν 'good in disposition' καὶ φιλοθεΐας ἔμπλεω τὴν διάνοιαν 'with mind full of love of God'. Προστιθείς 'adding' Num 18:19 Διαθήκη ἁλὸς αἰωνίου... σοὶ καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σοῦ, τηρεῖσθαι πάντως ἐκεῖνο προστέταχεν 'commanded that that be wholly kept' ὃ καὶ ἐν ἑτέροις ἔφη 'which he said elsewhere': Lev 2:13 Οὐ διαλείψει ἅλας διαθήκης Κυρίου ἀπὸ θυσιασμάτων ὑμῶν. Ἐπὶ παντὶ δώρῳ ὑμῶν προσ[οίσετε] [cont. 31].
